card.name: Wording that urges limiting or avoiding use
card.fires_on: The word right after a phrase that sets up a limit-or-avoid instruction, mainly "drugs" in "Reserve concomitant prescribing of these drugs". Also "if" before "possible", "be" before "avoided", and "minimum" in "Limit dosages and durations to the minimum".

modes.label: The instruction to reserve prescribing of these drugs
modes.description: The word "drugs" ending the opioid-with-CNS-depressant interaction instruction to reserve combined use for patients lacking alternatives.
modes.example: Reserve concomitant prescribing of these<< drugs>> for use in patients for whom alternative treatment

modes.label: The wording about avoiding or minimizing use
modes.description: Words in the middle of avoid-if-possible or limit-to-the-minimum phrases.
modes.example: Avoid concomitant use of torsemide and aminoglycoside antibiotics,<< if>> possible.

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words meaning "as little as possible", such as minimize and the Chinese equivalents of "try to".
card.plain: It responds to text where the label is about to say to keep use as low as possible or to avoid it.
